dedupe_keys.name: opendc open source cloud datacenter simulator

description: OpenDC is a free and open-source platform for cloud datacenter simulation, developed by the AtLarge Research group of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and TU Delft since about 2017. Its discrete-event engine models compute workloads, allocation and scheduling policies, power draw, energy use, carbon emissions and embodied carbon, checkpointing and failures of hosts in a datacenter topology. Failures can be switched off, replayed from a failure trace, taken from prefabricated models or sampled from three custom distributions, so availability and recovery under faults can be studied. Experiments are JSON files that name a topology, a workload trace, policies and export settings; results are Parquet files per host, task, power source and service, and the web interface gives automated plots. Coverage: any datacenter a user describes, with sample topologies and traces shipped for tutorials. Format and access: Kotlin and Java source on GitHub under the MIT licence, with documentation at opendc.org; releases up to v2.4u and commits in September 2026. Caveats: results depend on the traces and power models supplied; there is no physical cooling or electrical network model, and the web version needs a login. Simulation uses: capacity planning, energy and carbon scenarios, scheduling optimisation and resilience of datacenters to host failures. Related records: CloudSim Plus, CloudSim and SimGrid are other cloud and distributed-system simulators; the 2018 SC18 artefact on Zenodo is an early OpenDC release.
